Free speech is not the same as the right of free speech, which people are conflating in here.

Free speech is the ability to express ideas that may not be liked, favorable or kind without fear of "underhanded" repercussion. By underhanded I mean for reasons or in ways that are applied selectively and primarily due to bias and not the publicly stated rules of a community. An example of "underhanded" repression of free speech is how Reddit is dealing with topics on the legal troubles and history of Reddit CEO Ellen Pao and her husband. If any topic on them makes it to the front page, which numerous ones have, they get deleted. The threads are well liked by the community and there is no rule of the site that they're violating, Reddit is simply deleting them because they tend to paint their CEO and her husband in a less than flattering light. The reason they do this in an underhanded fashion is because they know that openly banning it would paint them as biased and against free speech, which is bad for their marketing themselves as a self styled "front page of the internet."

Some of the ideas mentioned that Voat plans to implement are the ability to display removed or deleted content from subs - presumably with some extremely rare exceptions for things like child porn. This stops the underhanded removal of topics since people can freely see what's being deleted, or directed by others to see what's being deleted, and then make a conscious decision whether or not they support that sort of suppression of information. This also stops people from misleading others on the reason things are being deleted.

Finally I'd add that free speech is not "often" debated. An extremely small minority of social justice extremists are, for the most part, the only ones opposed to free speech. This is in large part because their views don't tend to hold up under scrutiny so they prefer to simply ban scrutiny, but they're also wise enough to realize that creating rules that directly state "You're not allowed to question or speak negatively any of the things discussed here." would make them look like a cult. So instead they stick to underhanded means of enforcing said rule. People are free to block whatever sort of discussion they want, the important thing is that they make it clear exactly what sort of speech they're blocking. Another important part is not taking one reasonably sounding regulation and intentionally misapplying it. For instance, "No harassment." That's pretty simple and very few people would disagree with it. However, if I say "I think that's a bad idea because ...." I'm obviously not harassing you. Some individuals, again generally part of the social justice extremists, have taken to equating "No harassment" with "You're not allowed to question or speak negatively any of the things discussed here.".

TL/DR: Free speech is the freedom to say whatever you want within the clearly stated and nonambiguous rules of a locale without fear of repercussion.

Free speech means you are not subject to violence of any kind for transmitting or receiving information of any kind. There is no such thing as "abuse" because as soon as you discriminate against certain kinds of speech you cease to be in favor of free speech.

The idea(l) of free speech is old, but practicing (expressing AND excepting) can be more advanced or encouraged in some environments then in others (nationality, religion, upbringing).

So, in my opinion, we can modulate the rules to enable an environment for expressing one's mind in its absolute, but until the general population is ready to accept the resulting mindfuck it may encounter while letting it be, there's not much else to do but improve, fail, learn, and repeat the cycle. It will evolve.
